data.name: Vickram
data.gender_notes: Vickram is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Vickram is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vikrama', which means 'to be strong', 'brave', or 'valiant'. It is a name that symbolizes strength, courage, and victory over adversity. In Hindu mythology, Vickram is also the name of a king who was known for his courage and just rule. The name Vickram carries the meaning “Brave, Strong, Victor” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Vickram usually hope their child will grow to embody brave, strong, victor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Vickram represents the divine qualities of courage, strength, and victory. It is believed to bring blessings of inner strength, the ability to overcome challenges, and the power to triumph over adversity.
data.etymology: Vickram belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave, Strong, Victor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vickram total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Vickramaditya was a famous king of the Chalukya dynasty in the Deccan region of India. His reign is said to have lasted from 1096 to 1118 CE. He is known for his military conquests and his patronage of art and culture. During his reign, he extended the Chalukyan empire to its greatest extent, defeating the Western Chalukyas, the Kalachuris, and the Eastern Chalukyas.

Vyakranas Vickramaditya was a king of the Sangama Dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire in the late 15th century. He is known for his military campaigns against the Bahamani Sultanate and the Gajapati Kingdom of Orissa. He is also remembered for his patronage of the arts and his efforts to consolidate the Vijayanagara Empire.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Vickram' is of Indian origin and is associated with the legendary hero Vickramadithya from Hindu mythology. In modern contexts, this name is often seen in various media platforms that draw inspiration from this ancient folklore hero. On Television, there have been several adaptations of Vickramadithya's stories, such as 'Chandrakanta' and 'Vikram Aur Betaal'. In the Comics industry, Vickramadithya has been a popular character in Indian superhero comic books, with several publications featuring him as the protagonist. In the Gaming industry, Vickramadithya has been featured in several video games, such as 'Vikram and the Wishmaker' and 'Vikram Betal', where he is portrayed as an action-adventure hero.
